name: Aggressive phase pruning: 75%, 90%, and a non-entangling endpoint
cohort: All 64 previously inspected toy Module-LWE examples; exploratory adaptive extension, not a fresh holdout
endpoint_control: 100% removes all ZZ terms but keeps the fields and mixer. Its output is a product distribution that can be sampled classically; verify this explicitly.
primary_policy: Use unchanged EXP-003 shared angles and original normalization at all pruning levels.
secondary_policy: Retrain one shared angle pair per new fraction using the original expected cost on the same 16 separate public development instances.
quality_checks: Report both standalone optimum success and retained improvement in mean hybrid distance over Babai; 95% retention relative to full QAOA is a descriptive threshold. Also compare with the previous 50% setting and report individual losses.
rule: Remove floor(fraction * nonzero ZZ terms) by ascending absolute coefficient with lexicographic ties. Keep all fields, encoding, cost, initial state and mixer unchanged.

compilation.topology: all-to-all; no IBM device routing or calibration

limitations: Follow-up levels chosen after earlier development results; no confirmatory unseen-data inference or global best-pruning claim.
Removing terms changes the phase circuit, not the original decoding objective. It can alter the phase ground state and hurt particular examples.
Previously measured 0%-50% batches are retained; new 75%-100% batches use a new seed. Primary comparisons use exact ideal distributions, not observed batch rankings.
Babai already solves 53/64; overall hybrid success can conceal a decline in the extra quantum refinement. Report the retained distance improvement and recovered failures separately.
The 100% endpoint is classically samplable and has no entangling gates; its quality is not evidence of a quantum-specific benefit.
Gate counts are all-to-all compiled CX counts, not device durations, charged QPU usage, or noisy hardware performance.
One layer and one tiny parameter set; no practical ML-KEM attack, quantum advantage or novelty claim.
